feat(adminlock): admin.lock/server.lock protocol and locked offline init (W02.1b I) (#44)

* feat(adminlock): admin.lock/server.lock protocol and locked offline init (W02.1b I)

Implements the RW-C1 lock protocol (D01.3-r6 C.5.8 L1-L3, D01.4-r7 K16) in
internal/adminlock and runs offline init's database phase under it.

- L1: admin.lock is always taken before server.lock.
- L2 AcquireServerStart: admin.lock shared with a bounded wait
  (admin_lock_wait default 15m, 1-60m, outside the range refused),
  WAITING_ADMIN_LOCK logged every 30s, ADMIN_BUSY on timeout; then
  server.lock exclusive without waiting, SERVER_LOCK_HELD if held.
  ReleaseAdmin after classification keeps server.lock. A missing
  admin.lock is reported for the caller to classify.
- L3 AcquireOffline: admin.lock exclusive (created only by init, 0640),
  then server.lock exclusive without waiting, SERVER_RUNNING if held;
  both held until Close.
- admininit.Init takes the L3 locks, refuses database paths outside the
  data root, and holds both locks around ProvisionAndBootstrap. A loser
  returns before either database is opened.

Tests run real second processes (locktest) for the two-PID loser, the
start that waits behind an admin command, and ADMIN_BUSY.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(adminlock): annotate expected gosec findings

G304 on the fixed admin.lock/server.lock names inside the configured
directories, G115 on the fd conversion for flock, and G204 on the test
helper re-executing its own binary, using the repo's #nosec convention.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(adminlock): annotate G302 on server.lock mode and G702 on the test re-exec

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(admininit): resolve symlinks before checking data-root containment

Init's check that both database paths are inside the data root was
lexical. With root/link pointing elsewhere, root/link/jobs.db and
root/link/../jobs.db were accepted, and SQLite then created the
database outside the directory that server.lock guards.

Init now resolves symlinks in the data root and in each database path
before the check. An existing path is resolved whole, so a final
symlink is followed and a dangling one is refused. For an absent path
the raw parent is resolved without cleaning, because the kernel
follows a link before "..". Relative paths are made absolute the same
way.

Fixes the independent review finding G-L1 and Codex P1 r4322149017.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(adminlock): locate lock files on the kernel-resolved directory

filepath.Join cleaned the admin area and data root lexically, so a data
root spelled top/link/.. put server.lock in top/ while the kernel opened
the databases under the link target's parent. Init then passed the
containment check and wrote a database that a running server's
server.lock did not guard (pair review G-L1b).

lockPath appends the lock name without cleaning, for admin.lock and
server.lock in both AcquireOffline and AcquireServerStart. Regressions:
offline init and server start through link/.. meet the locks held under
the resolved directory and create no lock file elsewhere; an empty
directory still means the working directory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(admininit): pin resolved paths for the lock and every database open

Init resolved the data root and both database paths for its
containment check, but then took server.lock and opened SQLite through
the original paths. A symlink retargeted after the check could leave
server.lock held in one root while SQLite wrote through the link into
another root, where a second process holds a different server.lock.

Init now resolves the data root and both database paths once and uses
those resolved paths for the check, for server.lock and for every
database open in ProvisionAndBootstrap. Regressions retarget a link
right after the check: a data-root link swapped to a root whose
server.lock a running server holds (two processes), and a database
directory link swapped outside the root. The lock and both databases
stay in the checked root.

Fixes Codex P1 r4323139480.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(admininit): bind final database entries before SQLite opens them

Codex P1 r4323542522: for an absent database the pinned path is only a
pathname, so a symlink created at the final name after the preflight is
followed by SQLite while Init holds a different root's server.lock.

ProvisionAndBootstrap now holds each database file open from its first
open. An absent file is created empty with O_EXCL, which refuses a
symlink that appeared at the name (an empty regular file is PRISTINE,
so crash resume is unchanged); an existing one must be a regular
non-symlink file. Before and after every SQLite open each held path must
still name its held file, and no sidecar may be anything but a regular
file; otherwise ErrRefused.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(admininit): bind each database to the file the preflight inspected

GR-P2-HANDLE-1: a hard link or renamed-in regular file at an absent final name was bound and used, because bind fell back to a plain open on EEXIST and check only compared the path with the held file. ProvisionAndBootstrap now records both database paths (Lstat) before the preflight and requires them unchanged after it. bind creates a file the preflight saw absent with O_CREATE|O_EXCL and refuses EEXIST; a file it saw present is opened with O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK and must be a regular file, the same file (os.SameFile) and the same size the preflight saw, so an empty PRISTINE file must still be empty.

P3-AF: a FIFO at the name no longer blocks the open; the held file is refused unless it is a regular file.

Regressions: hard link at the absent ledger and authority names, rename-in over the empty ledger and at the absent authority name, a grown empty file, an authority appearing during the preflight (test hook SetAfterSee), and a FIFO (unix).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(admininit): refuse hard-linked databases and keep both bound through the markers

Codex review 6292389810 on fcee75b5 (three P1):

- r4325757882: an existing database with another hard link is refused
  (seeFiles, bind and every check). The other name may sit in another data
  root whose server uses the same file under its own server.lock.
- r4325757906: every database the preflight saw is bound at the first
  durable step, a SCHEMA_ONLY authority that no step opens too, and both
  are checked through the marker commit. An absent one is still created
  only by its own step, so a crash before it leaves it absent.
- r4325757865 (partial): the check after a step runs even when the step
  fails, so a replacement is reported instead of the SQLite error. SQLite
  still opens by path and keeps its sidecars by name, so a file swapped in
  between the check and SQLite's open can be written before the check
  after the step refuses. Closing that window needs a decision on the
  data-root trust model and is left to central.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(admininit): data-root trust for offline init (TRUST r4: I-T1, I-T2, I-G4)

Implements SORI-D01-TRUST-r4 (cf5e2dcd) as accepted with layout L-A,
option (a) and T2 (SORI-TRUST-20261021-R4-IMPLEMENTATION-ADMIT), the
data-root trust decision left open by Codex P1 r4325757865.

I-T1, G1 preflight: the data root and every directory down to a
database must be owned by the init principal, group sori, mode exactly
2770 (setgid, no sticky), with no extended or default ACL (the POSIX
ACL xattrs are parsed). Every ancestor must be owned by root, not
group/other writable and without a write ACL entry. Refusals are
retryable.

I-T2, installation identity: Init keeps <admin>/init-intent (temp,
fsync, rename, dir fsync; 0640). A first init refuses any existing
database or sidecar name durably and writes the intent first. Each
absent database is created O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, its identity tuple (dev,
ino, statx btime, inode generation where readable, uid, gid, mode,
nlink 1) is taken from the descriptor, the path is re-checked, the
coarse clock is waited past the birth time, and the record is made
durable before the descriptor is closed. A resume checks every
recorded file by the full tuple and accepts an unrecorded file only as
the C2 cut (empty, 0660, owner/group, born at or after
intent_created_at, P3-TR6). The database phase binds to the recorded
tuples, and both names and the installation id are checked against the
record afterwards. Identity and binding refusals write init-refused,
so a plain rerun refuses (INIT_REFUSED_STANDS) instead of adopting a
replaced file; I/O, lock, G1 and UNSUPPORTED_FILE_IDENTITY refusals do
not. A filesystem without birth times, and every non-Linux build, is
refused before anything is recorded.

I-G4: databases are created 0660 group sori (fchmod after create, so
the umask does not apply), and sidecars are left 0660 group sori.

The existing binding tests now drive ProvisionAndBootstrap directly,
because Init creates and records both files before the phase. New
Init tests cover G1 modes/owner/group/ACLs/ancestors, pre-existing
files and sidecars, a copied foreign pair, crash cuts C1-C5 and the
steps around them, the C2 birth-time rule, replaced/removed/moved
files, every tuple field, same-owner inode churn with the generation
ignored, the clock-tick wait, the descriptor held until the record is
durable, the phase bound to the record, the step-9 recheck, an
installation id changed in place, and tmpfs refused as unsupported.

Not done here: the explicit discard command (I-exit), the optional
server-start identity row (D-K), a second-uid server open, and
ext4/btrfs/overlay runs. Same-uid in-place writes and held
descriptors stay outside the model (TRUST r4 section 3.5).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* build: pin Go 1.26.10 for GO-2026-6809

crypto/x509 in the Go 1.26.9 standard library carries GO-2026-6809, fixed in 1.26.10. All workflows read go-version-file: go.mod, so the go directive is the only pin. No dependency or code change.

Refs #45

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* admininit: resume the pre-hand-over C2 cut and probe every database filesystem

A crash, or a failed chown or chmod, between the O_EXCL create and the G4 hand-over left an empty owner-only file that the rerun refused durably as unrecorded. The C2 cut now also accepts the owner-only create mode of a file the init principal owns, completes the hand-over on a descriptor checked against the observed identity, and records the 0660 tuple. A file swapped in between is refused durably.

Step 4a probed birth-time support only on the data root. A database directory on a nested mount without birth times let the intent and a database be written before the identity read failed. Each database directory is now probed before the intent or either file is written; the refusal is retryable.

Addresses Codex review comments 4335055244 and 4335055256.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* admininit: hold the recovered C2 file and wait past its birth tick until recorded

A resume that accepted a C2 cut recorded the file's tuple after closing
the descriptor it checked it by (owner-only cut) or without holding one
at all (0660 cut), and without waiting past its birth-time tick. A crash
after that record let same-owner churn reuse the freed inode within the
tick on a filesystem without a usable generation, and a later run adopt
the replacement (Codex P1 4338232085).

recordCut now holds the descriptor through the durable record and waits
past the birth time first, as createAndRecord does, at both cuts; the
held identity is checked against the first look for the 0660 cut too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* adminlock: create server.lock with mode 0660 under any umask

Codex P1 4339947250: os.OpenFile(O_CREATE, 0660) is masked by the umask (0022 leaves 0640), so a server of the sori group under another uid could not reopen server.lock read-write. openServerLock now opens an existing file as it is (mode untouched), and otherwise creates it with O_EXCL and sets 0660 on the open descriptor, only in the process that created it. A name that appears between the two opens is retried a bounded number of times; a dangling symlink is refused instead of followed.

Regressions: umask 022/027/077 on the offline and server-start paths, existing 0600/0640/0644 files keep mode and inode, a concurrently created file is not changed, a dangling symlink is refused and admin.lock released.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* adminlock: publish new lock files with their mode via a linked temporary file

Codex P1 r4340737885: init created admin.lock with O_CREATE, so a restrictive umask (0077) left it 0600 and a sori-group server under another uid could not open it. Codex P2 r4340737900: a crash between the O_EXCL create of server.lock and its fchmod left the name with a umask-masked mode that later opens keep.

Both lock files are now created under a temporary name in the same directory, given their C.5.8 mode (admin.lock 0640, server.lock 0660) on the descriptor, synced, and only then linked to the lock name; the temporary name is always removed. The name therefore never shows a file with another mode. Existing files keep mode and inode, a concurrent creator wins without a mode change, and a dangling symlink at either name is refused.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(adminlock): return temp cleanup failure after losing publication (Codex P2 4342525020)

openLock retried whenever publishLock's error wrapped fs.ErrExist. When the link lost the race and closing or removing the temporary name also failed, the joined error still matched, so the retry opened the winner's lock file and the cleanup failure and the .<name>.tmp-* residue went unreported.

publishLock now reports lost only when the link failed solely because the name exists; a close/remove failure clears it and is returned. Regressions: lost publication + read-only dir (EEXIST link, EACCES remove) for admin.lock by init and server.lock by offline/server start; a non-EEXIST link failure (EPERM) is not retried.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Adds internal/admininit.ProvisionAndBootstrap (RW-C1 §5.1/§5.1a). It inspects the job ledger and authority databases read-only and refuses before any write unless both are in an init-eligible state. Then it provisions missing known schemas through the version-pinned Open and chooses the installation id (16 CSPRNG bytes, 32 lower hex) only right before the single Init marker transaction. Compares the two database paths by file identity instead of by Abs string: two existing files by os.SameFile (hard links), two absent files by directory identity plus name (symlinked directories). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(admininit): compare raw parents so link/.. cannot alias one database (review B1)

When both database files are absent, sameFile compared filepath.Dir of each path. Compare the raw parents (the path up to its last separator, uncleaned) instead. Two new refusal cases, aliasing either path through a symlinked directory and "..", fail on the previous head and pass now.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Codex P1 r4314292550: when both files are absent, an authority path equal to
the job ledger's -wal (or -shm/-journal), or the reverse, passed the main-file
alias check. Opening the owning database then treated the other one as a stale
sidecar. checkPaths now also compares each main path with the other database's
-wal, -shm and -journal paths.

volume this is conservative.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

one file, so the authority schema was written and the job ledger then failed
against it after the disk had changed. sameFile now compares absent names
after NFC normalization and case folding, which also covers the SQLite
sidecar aliases. golang.org/x/text becomes a direct dependency at the
version already in the module graph.

Codex P2 r4320419157.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(admininit): refuse Win32 trailing dot/space and full case-fold absent-name aliases

Codex P2 r4321440348: a Win32 path open drops trailing dots and spaces, so absent names such as jobs.db and jobs.db. name one file there, but sameName kept them apart and both preflights reported PRISTINE. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(ops): land W02.1a contract facade

* W02.1a: restore sori.ops.v1 proto, pinned generation, provenance and internal jobledger facade

Restores the accepted D01.4 proto set (r3 blocks + r4 comment-only patch, unchanged through r7; proto_set_digest 5c91a0ec...f1ca) under api/, with the D01 buf.yaml (48de6bee...c75a) and the CAD-r2 local-plugin buf.gen.yaml. scripts/proto-gen.sh regenerates the Go code with buf 1.73.0 / protoc-gen-go v1.36.11 / protoc-gen-go-grpc 1.6.1 and writes a timestamp-free GENERATED.provenance; the new Proto workflow fails on drift or untracked output, and a Go test pins the accepted file hashes and set digest and rejects mismatches. buf breaking is not run: no accepted wire baseline exists yet.

internal/opsfacade reuses jobledger Accept/Lookup/GetJob behind fail-closed ports in the D01.4-r3 1.2 check order. Only FOUND carries a Job; refusals stop before any ledger call; effect/verification stay UNKNOWN. No server, Discover, RPC or CLI is exposed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* W02.1a: check D01.4-r3 golden fixtures in Go

Test-only reference encoders for the r3 1.1 envelope, the A.8 netstring and the B.2.2 namespace MAC reproduce M1-M8 (full sha256 and length), A8, NS1 (mac and 123-char token), NS2 and P1 (Discover bytes). X1, X2 and X4 reproduce their recorded short hashes and are rejected by the decoder rule. X3's exact bytes cannot be reproduced from the record, so it is checked for rejection only. The C# side is not executed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* W02.1a: bump golang.org/x/net to v0.60.0 for govulncheck

grpc v1.83.2 pulled in x/net v0.58.0, which govulncheck reports as affected by GO-2026-6617, GO-2026-6612, GO-2026-6611 and GO-2026-6603 (fixed in v0.60.0). go get raised x/sync, x/sys and x/text to the versions v0.60.0 requires. make vuln: no vulnerabilities; make test passes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* W02.1a: validate the idempotency key form and keep typed verifier reasons (B1, B2)

B1: the facade structure step now rejects an idempotency key outside the common.proto form (1..128 bytes of [A-Za-z0-9._~-]) with FIELD_INVALID before the namespace port or the ledger. B2: a Meanings error that is an *Error with MEMBER_KIND_REJECTED, TRANSFER_NOT_FROZEN, FIELD_UNKNOWN or FIELD_INVALID (also wrapped) keeps that reason; any other error stays RO_HOLD. The transfer-not-frozen test now expects the typed reason.

Also: negative cases for the meaning shape guard (31-byte digest, empty kind), timeout-minutes on the Proto job, and the provenance file name in two comments.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* W02.1a: refuse JobSpec unknown fields and drop stale generated stubs (P3-5, P3-1)

The facade structure step walks the JobSpec (nested messages, lists, map values) and returns FIELD_UNKNOWN for any unknown field before the namespace port, so an unseen field never reaches the meaning. proto-gen.sh deletes api/sori/ops/v1/*.pb.go before buf generate, so a removed .proto cannot leave a stale stub that gets hashed into GENERATED.provenance.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

authority: SQLite/WAL durable authority.Store adapter (W01.1, E016–E018) (#30)

* authority: SQLite/WAL durable authority.Store adapter (W01.1 slice1)

Add authority/sqlitestore, the J1 durable single-writer local profile
(SQLite/WAL on host-local disk). Every mutation runs in one BEGIN
IMMEDIATE transaction committed with synchronous=FULL before the result
is returned. It reuses the MemoryStore semantics and passes the
backend-neutral authoritytest suite including the Reopen tier. Export
authority.MembersEquivalent so adapters share one equivalence rule.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* go.mod: add modernc.org/sqlite v1.59.0 for authority/sqlitestore

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authority/sqlitestore: cross-process reopen and concurrent-writer evidence (E016, E017)

The test binary re-executes itself so each writer is a separate OS
process on the same database file. E016: state written by one process
(accept, bind, attach, locator and health change) reads back exactly in
another, and a changed-input retry there conflicts. E017: two processes
released by a file barrier produce one durable result for the same input
and exactly one winner plus a conflict for changed accept/bind/attach.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authority/sqlitestore: commit-boundary fault evidence (E018)

A child process SIGKILLed after its writes but before COMMIT leaves no
acceptance; one killed after COMMIT but before the ACK leaves exactly
the complete acceptance and a later retry of the same request returns
it. An in-process failure at the commit boundary rolls back bind and
attach entirely. Adds test-only commit hooks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authority/sqlitestore: satisfy lint (errcheck, gocognit, gosec G104)

Check the Close error on a failed Open and factor the record lookups
into one lookup helper, which also lowers BindAlias and
AttachRepresentation complexity. No behaviour change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authority/sqlitestore: extract bind target check; wrap long signature

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authority/sqlitestore: escape URI path; probe schema version before DDL

Open built the SQLite file: URI by concatenating the raw path, so a name containing ?, # or % was parsed as DSN parameters, a fragment or an escape (Codex r4238312356). fileURI now percent-encodes the path.

init ran this version's DDL before reading meta.schema_version, so a future schema without the current columns failed with a raw SQLite error instead of ErrSchemaVersion (Codex r4238312361). init now probes sqlite_schema first: DDL runs only on an empty database; an unversioned or other-version database is refused unchanged.

Tests: URI-significant directory names (journal_mode=wal, synchronous=FULL, exact file); future/unversioned/meta-without-version databases refused with schema unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* security: raise Go toolchain to 1.26.9 (sori#31)

go1.25.13 standard library is affected by GO-2026-6603, -6605, -6607,
-6608, -6610, -6611, -6612, -6613 and -6617 (crypto/tls, net/http,
net/textproto), all reachable from existing registry/dataspec code and
fixed in go1.26.9. Go 1.25 has no patched release.

CI setup-go reads go-version-file: go.mod, so this single directive
change moves every workflow to go1.26.9. go mod tidy produced no go.sum
change. govulncheck v1.1.4 (DB 2026-10-08) on ./...: 9 called findings
at go1.25.13, none at go1.26.9.

Refs #31

authority: backend-neutral authority.Store conformance suite (#28)

* authority: backend-neutral authority.Store conformance suite

Add authority/authoritytest with a reusable Harness{New, Reopen} and Run that every Store backend must pass: AcceptRevision idempotency/conflict/concurrent same RequestID, BindAlias append-only history order/idempotency/conflict, AttachRepresentation idempotency/conflict/member equivalence/list order, locator/health updates preserving Revision and Representation identity, and deep-copy fidelity. Reopen cases verify durability and are skipped as NOT IMPLEMENTED when Reopen is nil; MemoryStore runs the suite with Reopen=nil.

Suite self-checks reject deliberately broken stores. No durable adapter, shared staging, GC or J2 storage choice.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authoritytest: pin bind alias/asset, cross-revision attach and concurrent attach

Guardrail P2x3 on 6d3ebe5e (test-only):
- B2: same BindRequestID with a different alias or a different asset fails closed; both alias histories unchanged.
- C2: same AttachOperationID on a different RevisionID (identical format/proofs) fails closed; second revision stays representation-empty.
- C4: N=16 concurrent same-op attaches yield one RepresentationID and a list of length 1.
Each case has a matching mutant (alias-blind/asset-blind bind reconcile, revision-blind attach reconcile, duplicating attach) that the suite rejects.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* deps: bump oras.land/oras-go/v2 to v2.6.2 (GO-2026-6499, GO-2026-6497)

  Revision, not ErrRequestConflict.

  The retry must reconcile to the one Representation, and must not
  overwrite availability (locators/health) set since the attach.

presentation-comparing accept reconcile, locator-comparing attach
reconcile, availability-overwriting attach retry.

Test-only. Product authority package unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authoritytest: assert attach retry returns stored availability

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

  profile before reopen; after reopen a profile-only retry must return
  the original Revision.

  Alias or only AssetID changed must fail with ErrAliasBindingConflict
  and leave both histories unchanged.

  a second Revision with the same fingerprint must fail with
  ErrAttachConflict, add no relation and keep availability.

  asset-blind bind, revision-blind attach); the old suite accepted all
  four. revisionBlindAttach now returns the stored Representation on a

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Codex P2 4168216406: same RequestID with only builder identity, input lineage or member data format changed must return ErrRequestConflict, before and after reopen. Mutant: reconcile on (AssetID, member digests) only.

Test-only; product authority package and go.mod/go.sum unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

that uses those oracles, with and without reopen.

Addresses Codex review 4170842800 and 4170842807.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(authoritytest): ground revision oracles in the request and cover two-member paths

record the submitted AssetID and full Manifest (members compared as a
set), so a Store that consistently corrupts asset ownership or an

self-consistent. attachMatches checks the returned member proofs too.

AttachRepresentation/MultiMember cases round-trip a two-member Revision
and Representation, accept reordered retries as the same operation,

attach) or fail member equivalence (new attach).

Nine new mutants (asset/source rewrite, member truncation, first-member
reconcile/equivalence, order-strict reconcile) are each rejected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(authoritytest): pin second-member and second-proof rewrites

Adds two length-preserving broken-store mutants to TestSuiteRejectsBrokenStores: one rewrites only the second Revision member's proof digest on accept and read, the other only the second Representation member proof on attach, get and list. AcceptRevision/MultiMember and AttachRepresentation/MultiMember must reject them, so weakening the member-set comparison to a count check no longer survives the committed mutation suite.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(authoritytest): pin multi-member reopen, initial availability, algorithm and role identity

Reopen/MultiMember: a two-member Revision and a Representation carrying both proofs survive a reopen intact, and reordered retries after reopen reconcile to them. Lossy-reopen mutants (first member/proof only, second member/proof rewritten) pass every single-member Reopen case and are rejected only here.

Representation/AvailabilityPreservesIdentity now requires the first attach response to carry the submitted locators and the healthy state. AttachRepresentation/MemberEquivalence refuses the same digest under another algorithm with zero relations. AttachRepresentation/IdempotentRetryAndConflict retries with only the proof roles changed and requires the original Representation.

New broken stores: lossy reopen x4, initial availability dropped, digest-only equivalence, role-strict reconcile, role-echo retry. authoritytest only; authority package unchanged.

Addresses Codex P2 4171705114, 4171705116, 4171705118, 4171705120, 4171705123.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(authoritytest): pin algorithm reconcile and post-reopen member, proof and role identity

Reused attach operation with only the proof algorithm changed must conflict before member equivalence (Codex 4172000740). Reopen/MultiMember now also requires a post-reopen role-only retry to reconcile (4172000743), a second-member-only change under the same RequestID to conflict with the Revision unchanged (4172000744), and a second-proof-only change under the restored attach operation to conflict with the relation unchanged (4172000746). Four broken stores the previous suite accepted are now rejected: algorithm-blind attach reconcile, and restored first-member, first-proof and role-strict reconcile indexes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authoritytest: require algorithm-only conflict after reopen

Reopen/MultiMember now retries the restored attach operation with only a proof algorithm changed and requires ErrAttachConflict with the original relation unchanged. A backend that rebuilds its attach index from semantic keys and digests only passed the suite before (Codex 4176606947); the new restored-index mutant pins it. The other-algorithm literal becomes the proofAlgo2 fixture constant.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authoritytest: algorithm-only acceptance conflict and per-key proof association

Codex 4177013866 / 4177013873 on 23fc9d54 (authoritytest only):

- fingerprintOnlyConflicts (live and after reopen) also reuses req-1
  with only the member proof algorithm changed and requires
  ErrRequestConflict. Killed: algorithmBlindAccept (reconciles on the
  whole manifest except proof algorithms), live and restored.
- attachMultiMember swaps the two digests between m1 and m2, keeping the
  proof set: a fresh operation must fail ErrMemberEquivalence and the
  committed attach-multi must fail ErrAttachConflict; the relation count
  stays 1. Killed: keyBlindEquivalenceAttach and newKeyBlindAttach
  (unordered proof-set comparison).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authoritytest: swapped proof keys conflict after reopen

Codex P2 r4179704196: Reopen/MultiMember now reuses attach-multi with the existing proofs swapped between semantic keys and requires ErrAttachConflict; the final check keeps exactly one relation with the original identity. New broken store restoreKeyBlindAttach (restored attach index on the unordered proof set) passed the old suite and is now rejected. authority package untouched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
